status_split.note: From May 1994 the Palestinian Authority took over civil control of the Gaza Strip's towns under the Gaza-Jericho Agreement (signed 4 May 1994, Israeli withdrawal from about 60 percent of the Strip); Israeli settlements and military zones remained until the 2005 disengagement.

old_set.note: Captured by Israel in the Six-Day War (June 1967) and held under military occupation until the Gaza-Jericho Agreement of 4 May 1994.

cite.claim: Gaza-Jericho Agreement (signed 4 May 1994): Israeli military withdrawal from about 60 percent of the Gaza Strip, which covers Gaza City
cite.quote: It included an Israeli military withdrawal from about 60 percent of the Gaza Strip (Jewish settlements and their environs excluded) and the West Bank town of Jericho
cite.covers: the Gaza-Jericho Agreement and the Palestinian Authority takeover applied to the whole Gaza Strip, including Gaza City

cite.claim: The agreement transferred authority from the Israeli Civil Administration to the new Palestinian Authority
cite.quote: an agreement to a transfer of authority from the Israeli Civil Administration to the newly created Palestinian Authority
cite.covers: the Gaza-Jericho Agreement and the Palestinian Authority takeover applied to the whole Gaza Strip, including Gaza City

cite.claim: The Palestinian Authority became the governing regime in the Strip and received areas with civilian and security authority
cite.quote: Subsequently, the Palestinian Authority (pa) was established as the new governing regime in the Strip. Israel handed over some areas in which both civilian and security authority were transferred to the pa.
cite.covers: the Gaza-Jericho Agreement and the Palestinian Authority takeover applied to the whole Gaza Strip, including Gaza City

cite.claim: Arafat set up Palestinian Authority headquarters in the city of Gaza after 1994
cite.quote: Gaza held the limelight as Yasser *Arafat set up headquarters in the city of Gaza

set.founded_note: Founded as Nazareth Illit (Upper Nazareth); the Interior Minister signed the order renaming it Nof HaGalil on 26 June 2019. The older name is shown by governments.json city_names until then.

cite.quote: Israeli Interior Minister Aryeh Deri on Wednesday signed an order to officially rename the northern city of Nazareth Illit and changed it to Nof HaGalil

set.founded_note: Tarshiha is a pre-1948 Arab village (captured in Operation Hiram, October 1948); the Jewish immigrant town of Ma'alot was founded beside it in 1957 and the two merged into one municipality in 1963. Before 1963 the locality is shown as Tarshiha (governments.json city_names); the name Ma'alot-Tarshiha applies from 1963.

cite.claim: Ma'alot, an immigrant town, was founded in 1957
cite.quote: Ma’alot is an immigrant town 11 miles east of Nahariya that was founded in 1957.

cite.claim: Ma'alot merged with Tarshiha in 1963 to form a single municipality (before that the Arab village Tarshiha stood alone)
cite.quote: In 1963, Ma’alot merged with Tarshiha, a 900-year-old neighboring Muslim and Christian Arab village to form a single municipality.

set.founded_note: Construction began in 1963; the first families moved in on 10 September 1964 and the establishment of the city was announced at a ceremony on 29 October 1964.
